title: Host retirement handshake with soft telemetry fencing and weighted eviction
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput while hosts are retired for upgrades or replacement. Current drain/eviction flows cause transient throughput drops because traffic is shifted immediately or KV caches are cold. Goal: introduce a host retirement handshake protocol that safely offboards a host without violating throughput contracts by coordinating routing, autoscaler hedges, KV segment migration hints, and a telemetry-based fencing signal.
acceptance_criteria: 1) When a host enters RETIRE_PENDING the control plane issues a telemetry_fence flag; routing will reduce new request weighting to the host incrementally over a configurable window
2) Autoscaler automatically evaluates hedging reserves and, if needed, provisions a temporary capacity contract to maintain throughput SLOs during the offboard window
3) KV cache handshake endpoints allow per-shard prefetch tokens so peer hosts can pre-warm specific cache segments before the host goes SIGTERM
4) Observability shows less than 5% p99 latency regression and less than 2% request error increase during canonical retire scenarios in canary tests
5) All control messages and handshakes are idempotent and tolerant to network partitions; retries use commit token semantics documented in PR example
implementation_notes: High-level plan: 1) Add RETIRE_PENDING state in control-plane state machine; 2) Emit telemetry_fence to routing and downstream autoscaler; 3) Implement weighted-evict policy in balancer that reduces new-assign weight by 10% steps configurable per pool; 4) Add KV prefetch endpoints (/kv/handshake) and token lifecycle (issue -> ack -> transfer-complete); 5) Autoscaler will attempt short-lived capacity contracts (2-10 minutes) to hedge throughput during the handshake; 6) Implement canary in a single dedicated pool, validate metrics, then global rollout.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Autoscaler hedges cause cost spikes if retirements are frequent. Mitigation: cap hedging budget per pool and add backoff for repeated retire cycles (exponential backoff, metric: hedges_per_hour).
Risk: KV token leaks could cause stale transfers. Mitigation: token TTL + control-plane revoke path + audit logs; add tests that simulate network partitions.
Risk: Routing weight oscillation causing QoS jitter. Mitigation: hysteresis window and weight smoothing using decaying EWMA; integration tests to validate smoothing parameters.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): runtime-1.20-kv-canary group (5 hosts) - enable RETIRE_PENDING with telemetry_fence and kv-handshake endpoints; monitor grafana dashboard for p50/p95/p99 and errors; 48h
Phase 2 (limited pools): enable for non-critical dedicated pools with autoscaler hedging enabled; run for 7 days; validate billing and hedging logs
Phase 3 (global): enable across dedicated fleets with default soft_fence window of 300s and weighted eviction step 10%; incident playbook prepared
test_plan: Unit tests for state machine transitions and idempotent handshake messages
Integration test that simulates host retirement with pre-warm traffic replay and validates latency/error thresholds
Chaos test: partition control plane during handshake and validate safe fallback (host continues serving until explicit retire-confirm)
Load test: retire 10% of a pool under 80% utilization and verify autoscaler hedges prevent throughput loss
